title: CaCuTe: Casual Cubic-Model Technique for Faster Optimization

problem.claim: The work addresses faster optimization through adaptive switching between gradient and cubic-model steps.

contributions.claim: Establishes a local O(k^{-2}) rate for a gradient update under a 2H-Hessian–Lipschitz assumption.

Introduces regime detection using Hessian–vector products without forming or factorizing the Hessian, and incorporates the resulting certificate into cubic-regularized Newton and an accelerated variant.
Extends the technique to first-order, relaxed-smoothness, and stochastic settings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The technique achieved the lowest wall-clock time among the compared baselines in the experiments.
The method showed superior wall-clock performance despite backtracking.

narrative_sequence.summary: A gradient update is shown to have a local O(k^{-2}) rate under a 2H-Hessian–Lipschitz assumption.
Regime detection uses Hessian–vector products, and the certificate enables switching between cubic and gradient steps while preserving CRN's global guarantees.
Experiments report the lowest wall-clock time among compared baselines and superior performance despite backtracking.
The technique is described for first-order optimization, relaxed smoothness assumptions, and stochastic optimization.

source_observation.claim: Per-iterate switching between cubic and gradient steps can preserve CRN's global guarantees.

interpretation.claim: An adaptive hybrid optimizer may combine complementary update regimes while retaining the guarantees of a stronger base method.

application.claim: Use certificate-based switching when different optimization steps may be advantageous in different regimes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which switching is beneficial or how the global guarantees are derived.

source_observation.claim: Regime detection relies on Hessian–vector products rather than Hessian formation or factorization.

interpretation.claim: Matrix-free second-order information can reduce computational overhead in adaptive optimization.

application.claim: Prefer Hessian–vector products when adaptive curvature information is needed without explicitly constructing the Hessian.

exception.claim: The abstract does not quantify the Hessian–vector-product cost or identify settings where it is preferable to other curvature approximations.

unknowns: The compared baselines and experimental datasets are not specified.
The scope and derivation of the preserved global guarantees are not given.
The abstract does not provide detailed stochastic assumptions or convergence bounds.
